title: Permission ledger consolidation and staged RBACv2 cutover checklist
creator: Priya Nair
description: Consolidate permission ledgers and orchestrate a staged cutover from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with dual-write backfill, continuous reconciliation, and customer-facing communications. This ticket captures the operational checklist, validation harnesses, and fallback runbooks needed to complete a safe migration for hosted and Dedicated customers. Goals: preserve audit continuity, maintain SSO/SAML mapping correctness, avoid customer downtime, and provide a clear rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: All active accounts have RBAC v2-derived role mappings applied or an explicitly tracked exception
Backfill job completes for 100% of non-exempt resources within the staging window or is safely resumable
Dual-write telemetry shows under 0.1% divergence for a 72h synthetic-run sample before cutover
Audit events during and after cutover are tagged with migration-context and preserved in audit-forwarding stream
Customer-facing SSO mapping verification checklist available and executed for 10 pilot customers
backfill_strategy: Run two-phase backfill: Phase A (low-risk metadata + simple grants) then Phase B (resource-scoped grants and edge cases)
Backfill worker set isolated by customer tier; lower concurrency for trial/free accounts to limit DB pressure
Implement idempotent writers with progress tokens per customer to allow safe resume and parallelization
Record per-customer backfill status in migration ledger table with timestamps and reason codes
dual_write_strategy: Enable dual-write at API layer with transparent write routing to both v1 and v2 permission stores
Attach write-version header for tracing and enable sampling to capture paired write payloads to S3 for diff analysis
Run a nightly comparator job that reports divergent keys and operation types with prioritized triage queue
Expose a simple admin endpoint to rehydrate individual customer reconciliation on-demand
cutover_plan: Canary wave 0: Internal accounts + engineering org (24-48h synthetic + 24h real traffic)
Wave 1: 10 pilot customers (low complexity, read-heavy) with dedicated success criteria
Wave 2: 100 customers in batched waves by region and plan for automated rollback if divergence threshold exceeded
Global cutover: Rolling switch with traffic split (95% v2 routing) and 72h increased monitoring window
Emergency rollback: Flip routing to v1-only, mark affected customers, and start targeted reconciliation
verification_and_monitoring: Pre-cutover synthetic dry-run daily reports with tokenized sample requests covering SSO mapping permutations
Real-time divergence dashboard (counts, percent mismatch, top affected customer IDs) in Console -> Auth -> Migration
Audit-forward stream includes migration_context field and sequence id to enable forensic reconstruction
Post-cutover sampling: 1% of all auth events routed to deep-compare pipeline for 14 days
Automated alerting: Pager duty playbooks for divergence > 0.5% sustained over 10 minutes
comms_draft: Subject: Planned RBAC upgrade: Permission ledger consolidation and preview for pilot customers

Email body: We are upgrading our authorization system to improve reliability and auditing. You will see a brief period of enhanced checks but no expected downtime. If you have custom SSO claims or unusual admin scripts, please review the attached checklist. Pilot customers will receive invitations to test before broader rollout.
Admin console banner text: 'RBAC migration in progress: Some admin panels may show transient states. Contact support for anomalies.'
Post-migration status email subject: 'RBAC migration complete for your organization — action items (if any)'
github_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/402 - new monitoring dashboard and alert rules
kpis: Backfill completion rate per window (target 100% or logged resumable state)
Audit event continuity (no gaps > 1 second in audit-forward stream per customer during migration)
Number of customer-reported auth regressions (target 0 for pilot customers)
risks: Large-scale divergence due to edge-case SSO claim transformations
Unexpected load on DB indexes caused by backfill spikes
Customers with bespoke admin tooling that rely on v1 semantics
Audit log schema incompatibility with downstream SIEM connectors
mitigations: Add preflight SSO mapping checker and a one-click 'accept mapping' flow for customers with transformed claims
Rate-limit backfill per-customer and use queued workers with exponential backoff
Ship a temporary compatibility facade that responds to common v1 admin API shapes
Convert and forward audit events in dual format during a 30-day overlap window and provide translation adapters to SIEMs
